why: Integer cents and basis points avoid float rounding; invoice.py calls only these three functions.

value.region: customer region code as in data_tax/rates.csv, e.g. "TX". None or unknown region -> tax rate 0 (no error).
value.discount_pct: customer discount percent as Decimal or numeric string, e.g. "10" means 10 percent off. None -> 0.
value.lines: list of dicts {"category": str, "amount": Decimal|str} where amount = line total before discount and before tax. Category matched case-insensitively after strip against data_tax/exempt_categories.csv; exempt lines are excluded from the taxable base.
value.returns: Decimal total tax for the whole order, quantized to 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_UP. Computed once on the summed taxable base: base = taxable_sum*(100-discount_pct)/100; tax = base*rate/100 (rounded once, not per line).
value.errors: no exceptions for unknown region or category; malformed amounts raise ValueError.

why: Defines tax.py interface per RULES.md. invoice.py passes customer region/discount_pct from pricing.py and line categories/amounts; tax.py never computes item or customer data itself.

value: All monetary amounts are decimal.Decimal (or decimal strings like "12.50" at module boundaries). No float anywhere. Currency is USD, 2 decimal places, final rounding ROUND_HALF_UP.
why: Avoids float rounding errors in invoice totals and tax; needed by all three modules.

Two gaps. (1) Basis points cannot represent NY 8.875% (= 887.5 bp); use thousandths of a percent instead (8.25%=8250, 8.875%=8875, 10%=10000). (2) tax.compute(customer_id, subtotal, discount) cannot apply the exemption rule: tax.py needs per-line category, and tax.py has no customer data, so it needs the region passed in. value.units: all percents are int thousandths of a percent: 10% = 10000, 100% = 100000, 8.25% = 8250, 8.875% = 8875. All money is int cents (MONEY_REPRESENTATION v2).
value.region: str from pricing.get_customer(id)[region], e.g. "TX". None or unknown region gives rate_pm 0, never an error.
value.lines: list of (category: str, amount_cents: int). amount_cents = line total before discount and tax, from pricing.get_item(sku)[unit_price_cents] times quantity. A line is exempt if its category, stripped and compared case-insensitively, is in data_tax/exempt_categories.csv.
value.discount_pm: int from pricing.get_customer(id)[discount_pm]. None gives 0. Customer unknown means invoice passes region None and discount_pm 0.
value.tax_cents: int. taxable_cents = sum of amount_cents over non-exempt lines. base = taxable_cents * (100000 - discount_pm) / 100000. tax_cents = round_half_up(base * rate_pm / 100000). Rounded once over the order total, not per line. Returns (0, 0) when nothing is taxable or region is unknown.
value.errors: no exception for unknown region or category. Non-int amounts raise TypeError or ValueError.
